title: From papers to a TACO research agent
subtitle: Paper2Agent reading + CAUSEWAY implementation proposal
bullets: Meeting discussion • approximately 10 minutes
Goal: make research methods easier to inspect and use
Separate published findings, working software and future experiments
notes: Introduce CAUSEWAY as a research prototype with Patient, Doctor and Researcher views. Explain that this presentation first covers the paper, then our proposed application. The meeting date was not supplied, so no date is invented.

title: What does Paper2Agent contribute?
subtitle: Paper summary • preprint v2, October 2025
bullets: Connect a paper, its code and data to a conversational assistant.
Expose reusable functions through Model Context Protocol (MCP).
Test functions against reference examples before exposing them.
notes: MCP is a shared interface through which an assistant can discover and call functions. The conversational assistant and scientific function have different roles.
source: Paper2Agent v2, overview and extended methods: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.06917v2

title: How the paper builds an agent
subtitle: Paper summary • the reusable workflow
bullets: Locate code → configure environment → inspect tutorials.
Execute reference examples → extract tools → validate results.
Tools perform work; resources provide context; prompts guide workflows.
Connect the resulting server to an LLM-based assistant.
notes: A language model handles the conversation. Scientific functions handle calculations. This separation is the architectural idea we can apply to CAUSEWAY.
source: Paper2Agent v2, overview and extended methods: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.06917v2

title: Evidence and limits
subtitle: Paper summary • what the demonstrations establish
bullets: Case studies: AlphaGenome, TISSUE and Scanpy.
AlphaGenome: 15/15 tutorial queries and 15/15 novel queries correct in the reported benchmark.
These are selected computational benchmarks, not clinical validation.
Incomplete source code can prevent reliable tool creation.
notes: Treat these results as evidence for the demonstrated tasks, not a guarantee for every future scientific agent. The preprint and journal version differ; the figures on this slide refer specifically to preprint v2.
source: Paper2Agent v2, results and discussion: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.06917v2

title: Apply the idea to CAUSEWAY
subtitle: Our proposal • not an experiment reported in Paper2Agent
bullets: Researcher asks a question about TACO.
Assistant selects a documented tool and checks its inputs.
Tool returns structured evidence with source links and status.
Assistant explains the result and what remains unknown.
notes: Example: ask what data TACO requires. The assistant calls the TACO evidence tool, then explains the returned requirements. A tool response is like a labelled envelope: it contains the answer, its source and whether an analysis actually ran.

title: First TACO agent: a small useful start
subtitle: Our implementation scope
bullets: Retrieve TACO purpose, input requirements and limitations.
Check whether a proposed data manifest is complete.
Expose tools, a reference resource and a workflow prompt via MCP.
Prediction execution remains unavailable until the upstream pipeline is reproduced.
notes: A manifest describes a dataset without sending its measurements. Our first version checks this description. It does not establish that the data are biologically suitable. An MCP host supplies the language model; the website exposes the same evidence tools without claiming to be an LLM chat.

title: Patient Portal: add useful context
subtitle: Requested feature • fictional demo data only
bullets: Comorbidities: other conditions a person has.
Current medicines: name, dose, frequency and reason for use.
Distinguish no conditions/medicines from information not supplied.
Show the same session context to the doctor.
notes: For example, the fictional case can include asthma and a current medicine. These entries help explain what information a future clinician might review. In this prototype they stay in browser memory and do not change a TACO prediction.

title: Researcher Portal: compare the methods
subtitle: Requested feature • keep each task distinct
bullets: Causal discovery: MR, Control Theory and DCE.
Subtyping: expression-based clustering with symptom interpretation.
Early detection: TACO, combining selected genes and TabPFN.
Drug research: SPLIT, using cohort-specific predictions.
notes: Each row needs inputs, outputs, a source and an implementation status. A gene association, a cluster and a prediction probability answer different questions. We must not combine them into one invented confidence percentage.
source: Project module catalogue and linked upstream studies

title: How can methods be combined?
subtitle: Our experiment planning tool
bullets: Select methods and inspect the proposed combination.
Check shared gene identifiers, cohort definitions and data requirements.
Label published pipelines separately from proposed combinations.
Compare methods with task-specific metrics and independent validation.
notes: A combination is a research recipe, not a result. Selecting ingredients does not prove that they work together. Methods may use incompatible tissues or cohorts, and reusing the same dataset can make an apparent comparison overly optimistic.

title: Doctor Portal: explain what is visible
subtitle: Requested feature • interpretability
bullets: Show which selected symptoms match each displayed research theme.
Show the rule, its source and its limitations.
Keep comorbidities and medicines visible as context.
Show model explanations only after a model has actually run.
notes: Interpretability means helping the reviewer understand why the interface shows something. For today's symptom themes we can show the exact checkbox rule. We cannot show patient-level feature attribution or SHAP values from a model that has not run.
source: Local design: Doctor Portal explanation panel

title: Keep the Shiny application in the workflow
subtitle: Key resource supplied by the project team
bullets: Open the existing Shiny explorer from the Researcher Portal.
Use the associated paper to understand its MR/CT results.
Keep external exploration separate from locally executed analyses.
Live Shiny contents still need checking; the research browser could not open the site.
notes: The supplied address is an important reference. Add a prominent external link and explain what the associated publication describes. Do not imply that CAUSEWAY has imported the live results or can execute the Shiny application.

title: What the team should decide next
subtitle: Meeting discussion
bullets: Which TACO commit, preprocessing and model artifact are authoritative?
Which reference dataset and expected outputs will verify reproduction?
Which method combinations should be tested first?
Who will review the scientific interpretation and future patient-data workflow?
notes: End with concrete decisions. The immediate research milestone is reproducing one agreed TACO example and comparing its output with the authors' reference. After that, expose the verified prediction function through the same agent interface.
source: Team discussion • no clinical deployment proposed
